Cyclone is Michael DeLaFleur's second collection of instrumental songs.  It is great music to take for a drive in the car, full of sound pictures that can keep your brain occupied 110%, or exist as a perfect background soundtrack to your adventures.  Like a cyclone, the music is powerful and somewhat unpredictable at times, with moments of calm interspersed.    Cyclone has various musical winds spinning around its eye, blending a bit of techno, alternative and a DJ's sampling and looping mentality with riff rock, progressive rock and even disco. Diverse influences from Moby to Yes to REM to Steve Hackett meld into something completely new yet intimately familiar.     Below are two in-depth reviews of Cyclone from [...].    Review by Rhonda Readence  Rating:  5 stars (out of 5)    Michael DeLaFleur, who writes all his own material, plays all the instruments, and recorded and engineered the album Cyclone, is out to prove to the music world that he is a master of his domain.  All the proof anyone needs is contained in his 14-track sophomore album titled Cyclone, a brilliant instrumental soundscape of relaxation, serenity, and tranquility.    The album begins with \\"Dance,\\" a 54-second track with a funky vibe that is a nice introduction to Michael DeLaFleur and the sound he has created.  The opening track rolls smoothly into \\"Hi Volume,\\" a beautifully composed piece of melodic instrumentation.  The sound is exceptionally clear and precise, and if this track is any indication of the sound quality throughout, listeners are in for a treat.  The title track, \\"Cyclone,\\" opens with the soothing sounds of a thunderstorm and then bursts into magnificent guitar playing that showcases Michael's diversity.  Heavier riffs that bring to mind Black Sabbath are coupled with flowing melodic hooks that defy categorization.  The song builds in intensity much like a cyclone does, until it ends with the graceful sound of falling rain.      \\"Orange Sky\\" carries a melody that is hauntingly familiar, yet one would be hard pressed to put a finger on exactly what it is reminiscent of.  With a sense of familiarity and tranquility, this piece is comfortable and warm.  Michael's piano playing is light and confident, the instrumentation is flawless, and the sound quality is absolutely inspiring.  While listening to this piece, it is entirely possible to feel completely relaxed and whole.  \\"Peace Maker\\" also has a sense of familiarity to it, as if it is an old favorite, even to listeners who are hearing it for the first time.  There is a melancholy feel that will tug at the heartstrings, but at the same time, it offers a sense of confidence and strength.  This track can actually be an exercise in mediation, if listened to with eyes closed and an open mind.  \\"Boom!\\" begins with an extraordinarily melodic rhythm that will remain in the head for hours after hearing it.  One of the most intricate pieces on the album yet with regards to sound quality, this one will surely be a fan favorite.  \\"Boom!\\" is beautifully addictive and hauntingly creative.      Cyclone spins onward with \\"The Dragon Awakens,\\" a track that feels a bit out of place on this album and not as pleasing to the ear as the preceding offerings.  The bass line is slick, the musicianship and sound are incredible, but one must wonder if the vocalization is necessary.  At times it seems to be a bit much, and at others it is the perfect touch.  Perhaps Michael needs to pick and choose where to add the vocals and where to remove them.  Overall, the piece is melodic and inspiring with a relaxing rhythm that has a spiritual essence about it.  \\"Blue Ridge Sunrise\\" speaks of the mountains that Michael DeLaFleur grew up looking at in Front Royal, Virginia.  A beautiful piece of the country that inspires a beautiful song, \\"Blue Ridge Sunrise\\" encompasses nature's gifts and Michael's own into a pleasing harmony of expertly played guitar and incredible composition.  A song that allows the mind to journey into the gorgeous Blue Ridge Mountains as the sun graces the day, this piece is another wonderful example of music that could be used to enter a higher state of consciousness through the art of meditation.      \\"Maxifunkilicious\\" starts off just as the title suggests: with maximum funk.  It's got a beat with attitude that will get the feet tapping.  As usual, the sound quality is stellar and this tune has a bit of jazz, some soul, and all funk.  \\"Kitty Mama Theme\\" is an odd one.  Listeners with cats will love this track, and perhaps so will their cats.  Excellent instrumentation is coupled with the meows, purrs and mews of cats and kittens.  It's rather cute and cuddly with a catchy, happy beat that will bring smiles.  \\"Intuition\\" is another signature Michael DeLaFleur masterpiece with incredible sound production, excellent musicianship and precise composition.  This piece flows exceedingly well and showcases Michael's talents as writer, composer, musician and engineer. Well done.     \\"I Didn't Inhale\\" carries a sense of humor with sound bytes of Bill Clinton's famous line.  For the stoner in all of us, this psychedelic offering will bring a twisted smile to the face.  Michael does a fantastic job with the loops and samples in this piece.  It is intricate and there are many layers to this song that sit beautifully, one atop the next.  This piece is art, pure and simple.  \\"Tidal Forces\\" picks up the tempo a bit and there is a spectral feel to this one.  Michael's flair for the dramatic comes forth in this track as the rhythm rises and falls and then rises again.  He keeps it all moving smoothly and this is yet one more example of the artistic creativity harbored in the mind of this musician.    Cyclone closes with \\"Just For Fun,\\" a slower tune with some Santana-like guitar work that will leave listeners in awe.  In Michael DeLaFleur's bio, he states, \\"he can't sing well but that hasn't stopped him yet.\\"  What Michael DeLaFleur does do well is write and compose music, play every instrument that needs to be played, and engineer and produce some of the finest sounding music in the world today.  With talents like that, being able to sing suddenly doesn't seem all that important after all.      Review by Matheson Kamin  Rating:  4 stars (out of 5)    Musician Michael DeLaFleur has followed the 2009 release of Realization with 2010's Cyclone. With his new release, DeLaFelur takes a rock base and combines it with many different genres to create different styles for the numerous tracks on the CD.    To start the Cyclone CD off, DeLaFleur created a short track entitled \\"Dance\\". \\"Dance\\" has enough of a beat that anyone who wanted to could get up and move, but it would he short-lived, as the track that doesn't quite hit one minute.  Next comes \\"Hi Volume,\\" and  finds DeLaFleur combining  rock and jazz into one enjoyable song, and the sound byte \\"This should be played at high volume\\" adding depth.    The title track, \\"Cyclone,\\" is one of the hardest rocking songs on the release. Here, DeLaFleur's guitar playing brings to mind other guitarists like Vai or Satriani.  While \\"Cyclone\\" is one of the hardest songs on the album, the following track, \\"Orange Sky,\\" is quite the opposite. Featuring DeLaFleur on acoustic guitar rather than electric, it is a nice contrast to the harder songs that are found on the release.  Once \\"Orange Sky\\" has come to a close, the album gets heavy again on \\"Peace Maker\\". \\"Peace Maker\\" is one of the best demonstrations of DeLaFleur's skills a composer.  \\"Maxifunkilicious\\" is the most apropos title on Cyclone. The song finds DeLaFleur showing off his skills in creating music with a funky beat.    On the most unusual track of the release, \\"Kitty Mama Theme,\\" DeLaFleur has taken real life sounds from cats, including purring and meowing, and added these sounds into the body of the composition. At points, it sounds like the cats are actually singing along with the music. As far as the music for the track is concerned, the oriental-flavored rock music that DeLaFleur composed to use as a bed for the cats is well written and really could easily have stood on its own if DeLaFleur had chosen to leave it alone.  To add a little bit of humor to the album, Michael DeLaFleur took one of the most famous quotes in the nineties and created a song around it. The \\"I didn't inhale\\" quote from President Clinton is used to create a humorous effect on the track by the same name. Now, if only DeLaFleur had kept the track of \\"I Didn't Inhale\\" under six minutes. The nearly ten-minute track ended up beating a joke to death.     On \\"Tidal Forces,\\" Michael DeLaFleur blends a steady beat with a bit of a techno edge to create one of the most unique tracks on the album.  To bring Cyclone to an end, DeLaFleur included the song \\"Just For Fun.\\" Since the track is just over a minute, the short, jazz-like song leaves the listener wanting more.     To create the album, Michael DeLaFleur played all of the musical parts. The album proves that DeLaFleur is not only a talented songwriter, but he also is a talented musician, as well.  Altogether, the many different styles of music on the Cyclone release from Michael DeLaFleur blend together to form one solid release that has enough variety in it to please anyone, no matter what style of music you most prefer.

The CD package artwork (or just the \\"cover\\" image for the MP3 edition) is a clear indication of the audio \\"content\\" of this album. The front depicts a human brain with primitive electrodes stuck into it; the rear of the jewel case is but musical staves with EEG squiggles across them; the inside of the booklet shows an overly-halftoned color image of a surgically-exposed brain with a plastic plate of electrodes being laid onto it. There is no \\"music\\" whatsoever on this album - only computer-generated sounds which could conceivably come from electronic appropriations of thought-patterns during the course of everyday life. The only other of Steve Fitch's recent albums to which this compares would be the one by Kleinabermein (his side project of sorts), although the sounds on that album are of quite a different nature and atmosphere. At 39 minutes, this album is \\"short,\\" but is a perfectly-timed intense experience. This modern \\"noise\\" music is unusual for its not trying to sound harsh all the time, and in fact, some of it is gentle or playful.

I've been a fan of trailer music for a long time and enjoyed Thomas's work in Two Steps from Hell as well as that of  similar artists such as The Immediate. This is my favorite album of the Epic Music genre. Thomas works in a lot of different emotions  and character in these songs, and with nineteen songs, there's something for everyone.    Musically speaking, what stands out in Illusions is the use of fantastic female vocalists that will send a shiver down your spine. Latin-type choirs are here, as well, but more judiciously applied than in some of the other trailer-type music that tends to overdo it. Thomas employs  pulsing strings, heroic horns, and driving beats, and he uses these to create story-scapes in your mind.    Stand out tracks: Starvation (feels like you're in a mine with scrawny slave children), Ocean Princess (standing on a cliff watching a mighty, rescuing ship pull into view), Homecoming (you've died and gone to heaven. Chills every time. Great medicine for a bad mood), Immortal (a warrior cleaning up on the battlefield) and Age of Gods (Heroes facing down the hordes. The mirroring of the horn and latin choir at the beginning are chill inducing).    There are no bad tracks on the album. Even the ones with a softer touch (Remember Me and Hurt) are a fun listen. Nine bucks is a ridiculously low amount to pay for this much quality music, so enjoy.

If you're reading this, then you're probably wondering if you should buy the two shows above in digital form, because you already know what's going on here and you need that extra push because it's kind of a steep price. Well, you should buy it, because of a couple reasons. First, this is mid-82 Black Flag, when they were at their absolute rawest and hungriest, touring in a van held together by duct tape, eating table scraps and sleeping on sandpaper floors stained with motor oil. Second, the lineup was peak: Chuck Biscuits was apparently new to the band by a week or so, but you'd never know it from his insane performance here. Rollins is on fire: he's yelping, screaming, lunging, looking at people and ripping them apart. The band, although no more than a train of controlled noise on this tape, is crushing and abrasive. Third, this is sort of a lost gem: the shows aren't even mentioned in \\"Get In The Van\\", and the set lists cut pretty deep. I was astounded at the song choices and bought it based on that alone and a quick listen to make sure it was a good audio. (Those who think otherwise have zero experience with live punk rock recordings, and I'll say straight-up that expectations of \\"better sound quality\\" are misplaced because this sounds top-notch for an '82 live hardcore show.) So basically, you know what this is, you know who it is, it sounds great, and if you spend a day or two with it, you'll find that in many places it's better than you thought, and eventually throws your gut at the world. More than you know.

review_headline: Classic performance, but mp3 file issues.....
review_body: This performance is a known quantity, having been in release in some form or another for nearly 60 years.  If you search out other reviews, you can get more info on its importance and historical background.  This is an inexpensive way to download this historical recording.  Not having heard other incarnations of it, I will assume that this is a straightforward transfer from the original Decca recording, and the overall sound is quite acceptable for early 1950s monaural.  The long tracks (while helping to make it an expensive buy) may make it inconvenient to access certain points in the opera.  This still is preferable to my mind than having a bunch of mp3 tracks with the annoying breaks between them that typical mp3 players create.  The PROBLEM with this recording is that there are several instances (e.g. in the last track, Act III, but elsewhere) where the recording has been truncated, and some portion of the music has been lost.  I don't know the opera well enough to know HOW many seconds are lost in each truncation, for which I'd have to follow the libretto to get an idea, but it's noticeable and jarring.  Whoever made this transfer didn't listen to it afterwards, or this would have been caught.  For that reason, I can't really recommend this download, because of the incomplete and truncated transfer to the mp3 files.

These guys are an economical, muscular combo who craft really catchy tunes. It's got all the elements of a classic power pop record -- big easy hooks, crunchy guitars, classic-rock riffs, and a slight new wave slant -- but without getting too locked into that early 80s sound that most purveyors of the genre seem to be stuck in. Part of that is in the retro-rock riffs that crunch more than they jangle (more Keith Richards than Tommy Keene), part of it is in the beefier production that doesn't sparkle so much as it punches.     Lyrically they're not too serious -- one song is about Summer Glau? -- but like some of the best rockers they have a slightly skewed view of the world. In this case it's a dorky one, I guess that's what \\"nerdwave\\" is. Overall, it's a fun album and you could do worse if you're looking for catchy rock and roll.

review_headline: The New Heathens - New York City Roots
review_body: Recently the mailbox was blessed with a CD by a band from New York called the New Heathens. Not to be confused with Band of Heathens but equally as good, totally different in sound and with some luck maybe as successful. \\"Hello Disaster\\" will floor you. Truth be told  during the 1980's the Del Lords, the Smithereens, the Rave-Ups et. al. were \\"real\\" alt-country staples. The fact that Eric \\"Roscoe\\" Amble, guitarist for the Del Lords, produced and played some tasty guitar on `Hello Disaster' may have something to do with why this has become a staple today. Not since the Bottlerockets `Radar Gun' has Americana roots music that rocks like this. And rock it does; from the opening note to the last. Nate Schwebber's vocal's ebb and flows with the album's mix of beer soaked rock and roll and cool country rhythms. `Hello Disaster' has more hooks than a tackle box and more ways to bait you in.     The new heathens  There is something about the unbridled joy of playing rock'n'roll. The first chords and beats that come together in a basement or garage start in motion a ball that will keep moving as long their is momentum. For some, the garage disappears a bit as time moves on and playing is perfected. For others, they clearly develop move of a mastery of instruments but never lose that heart pounding, beat driven simplicity that is the calling card of the Big R, little n, Big R. That memory, and ability to craft three/four minute power punches, is the stuff that drives New Heathens sophomore album effort, 'Hello Disaster\\".    It rattles and rolls (\\"Feelin' Lucky Again\\", \\"27 Years\\"), glides and shuffles (\\"Thankless War\\", \\"Only gets Better\\" and burns rubber (\\"Crybaby\\", \\"Proud Highway\\"). Whether the electric becomes acoustic (\\"Bastard Like Me\\") or the pound of the beat gently sways (\\"I Thought You Were My Friend\\"), 'Hello Disaster stays close to the garage electrical outlets that housed the jangle of 60's guitars. For New Heathens, that works. The band brings the best of the finalfour decades of the last century and shines them up with their own sound stamp.

review_headline: Tim at his best with his favorite theme
review_body: Ah, what a joy to hear this album. I have been a fan of Cursive and The Good Life for a awhile now. The Good Life has always put out good work musically on the subject of couples. The Good Life's past two albums Help Wanted Nights and Album of the Year; you should check out if you are a fan of this album. But I think Tim finally to me has made his most coherent album on the theme of couples and the desperation couples end up in. There's a lot of honesty in all of his writing. There are moments which are humorous and tragic at the same time on this record. I feel he captures these moments and others brillianty on this album, which i always missed before on his other works. This album is as sharp as a knife. Strays is one of Tim's most uplifting songs, which says a lot of how much he has grown. I think it's was perfect timing for him to have a self-titled record. Maybe it inspired him more, who knows. So very happy for the artist and to have listened to him grow. Don't miss out on this one, it truly is one of the best of 2010. Worth every minute. I hope more people catch onto this artist.  If you want to try a song or two to see if it's for you. Try strays or cold love.

The best tracks are those which remain faithful to the original tunes, such as Karen Elson's \\"Crying, Waiting, Hoping,\\" Jenny O's \\"I'm Gonna Love You Too,\\" The Detroit Cobra's \\"Heartbeat,\\" and especially Cee Lo's \\"(You're So Square) Baby I Don't Care,\\" but they're outnumbered by trainwrecks like Florence + the Machine's \\"Not Fade Away,\\" Reed's \\"Peggy Sue,\\" and Fiona Apple's \\"Everyday.\\" I really wish those iconic classics had been entrusted the lesser artists like Jenny O and Karen Elson who would've treated them well.

My Best Theory is the lead single to Jimmy Eat World's upcoming album, Invented. It's an enjoyable song, but doesn't measure up to the band's previous offerings. Bleed American, Pain and Big Casino were clearly better as lead singles. This is definitely a new sound for them, but it's one that inspires mixed feelings. I would recommend the song as whole, but I would bet that the weak chorus prevents the song from getting a great deal of radio airplay.    Many say that nearly every band makes their best music within a 7 year span. From Clarity (1999) to Futures (2005) I loved Jimmy Eat World's music. Chase This Light was a definitive step back, while My Best Theory indicates that Invented might just tread water. Despite its failure to measure up to previous hits from the band, it's still a song that belongs in your library.

review_headline: Frontline members deliver a melodic hard rock dinamite in 2004 with Carsten Schulz at the helm!!
review_body:
\\"Tatooed heart\\" is the second studio album by German melodic hard rock band \\"Evidence one\\" originally released in 2004. At the time \\"Frontline\\" members, guitarist Robert Boebel, drummer Rami Ali and bassist Thomas Bauer would regroup with lead singer Carsten Schulz (\\"Domain\\", \\"Midnite Club\\") and guitarist Wolfgang Schimmer.

2004 also sat the release of the 7th \\"Frontline\\" studio album, therefore one could reasonably question how focused was this second studio effort by \\"Evidence one\\". Truth is that \\"Tatooed heart\\" is an incredible melodic hard rock album with a metalic flavor to it. As everything carying the siganture of Robert Boebel, the album benefits from incredibly thick and polished production; from there onwards the melodies come in plenty, the solos are more extensive while Carsten's vocal performance is technically impeccable and passionate as always. Favortie tracks include \\"Virus in my veins\\", \\"written in blood\\", \\"When thunder hits the ground\\" and \\"Tattooed heart\\".
The overall sound of the album could easily be characterized as arena hard rock, simply because everything on \\"Tatooed heart\\" sounds immense. One could use the term overproduced on the album, still a hard rock fan would rarely complain for a band's devastating drum sound or plethora of melodic guitar lines. If you enjoy melodic hard rock produced to the maximum, filled with decimating choruses, titanic rhythm section and endless melodic attack you should definitely get \\"Evidence one-Tattoed heart\\" as well as trying Boebel's other bands namely \\"Frontline\\", \\"State of rock\\" and \\"Sanction X\\".

review_headline: A few solid songs, but mostly meh.
review_body:
I come to this as an outsider - I have previously listened to a few Arcade Fire songs (or watched videos) because of friends who like them. There was a lot of build up to this release, so when I saw it was only $3.99 I thought I would check it out with little to loose. Just because I won't give it 5 stars, some will hate this review - fine, but this is my honest opinion.

I really wanted to like this album. But I'm not an uncritical fanboy, so I can't. Sure, I don't hate it, it isn't bad. But it isn't special like some would have you believe. Don't drink that Kool Aid blindly.

My favorite part of the album as a whole is the overall ebb and flow of pace and style that keeps it at least interesting and listenable. It is music you can put on while driving down the road, and then tune out while you think of something else. But that isn't what I want in my music. I want it to grab me, to change me, to make me feel something, but mostly all I get from this is indifferent meh.

Some of the tracks really seem like they are trying to hard to be different. There is nothing wrong with different, but being different just to be different almost never works out unless your name is Beck.

1. The Suburbs - solid start, creative and catchy.
2. Ready to Start - R.E.M. does this better. So did The Cure.
3. Modern Man - It's like they stole it from 80's Devo and modernized it. Not bad!
4. Rococo - I like the rich musical sound, but the vocals don't add to it.
5. Empty Room - U2 meets Bjork. Not bad, but not great either.
6. City With No Children - U2 does this so much better.
7. Half Light I - Modern Pink Floyd - really good!
8. Half Light II (No Celebration) - Kinda Faith No More cross with INXS - and I really like it!
9. Suburban War - a modern take on acid rock? Wanted to like it, but can't.
10. Month of May - This one should be really high energy in concert, but doesn't seem to translate on the album.
11. Wasted Hours - Love it! Catchy, makes you want to air strum along.
12. Deep Blue - This is the rich sound like Rococo, but I like it much better. The vocals add to it here. Probably my favorite track.
13. We Used to Wait - Like the lyrics, you can keep the music.
14. Sprawl I (Flatland) - Good emotional \\"feeling\\" song. Easily blends into the background of life.
15. Sprawl II (Mountains Beyond Mountains) - Ace of Bass? ABBA? Really?
16. The Suburbs (continued) - Like Neil Young might sound today if he were 35 years younger. And that's a good thing. Great end to the album.want to air strum along. 12. Here, Taiwanese/American pop singer, Kris Phillips (aka Fei Xiang), performs a song from Andrew Lloyd Weber's \\"Jesus Christ Superstar.\\" I've seen the video of the performance, and the visuals are not outstanding, but Kris's vocals are always perfect. He has a flawless, ethereal, expressive tenor.

For those of you who do not know, Kris is the lead recording artist of mainland China, but is virtually unknown here in the US. This is a mysterious thing, really. This great superstar, so unknown in one of his home countries, despite the rumors that he lives most of the time in New York City. Kris said in an interview in China that he attributed his lack of success in the US to racism.

That could be true. People tend to buy recordings by artists of their own ethnic/racial/religious group and there aren't that many Asians here.

On the other hand, it could be that Kris's style is one that has been out of vogue -- more like the styles of singers in the 1940's than like that of contemporary singers. Still, as classical/pop crossover is getting bigger now, it seems that people should pay attention to Kris's work. He really has a stellar voice.

It's too bad that most of his Chinese language albums are not readily available in the US. Music is an international language and his singing is beautiful whether in English or Chinese. I believe he is at least tri-lingual (English, Mandarin, Cantonese) but this particular recording here is in English.

For those of you who have never seen him perform, check out the website of his Brazilian fan club, or videos they have posted of him on YouTube. He looks something like Vulcan, or an elf from Lord of the Rings -- very tall (6'4\\") and slender, with Asian eyes & hair, but western build & facial shape -- extremely handsome -- a striking figure in any culture.

Kris has acted as a sort of self-appointed friendship embassador from Taiwan to China and sang very idealistic songs at the 2008 Beijing Olympics and the 2010 World Expo in Shanghai. He's definitely a change agent -- being part of the opening of China to the world -- and promoting international understanding. He is highly underappreciated.e 2010 World Expo in Shanghai. review_headline: Six Nations Ontario Canada's Hardest Working Band
review_body: These guys were at one time the most wanted all native bar/dance band in the land. In 2005 they appeared on Canadian televisions Aptn Rez Blues and after being together for 15 plus years finally decided to write record and release an album of original material ( Beg, Borrow & Steal by Matt Minglewood being the only cover). This record before you garnered the band nominations at native music festivals including, Indian Summer Music Awards, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Canadian Aboriginal Music Awards, in Toronto, Ontario. Aboriginal Peoples Choice Music Awards, in Winnipeg, Manitoba and North American Music Awards (NAMMYS) in Niagara Falls, NY. Sadly they disbanded in 2009 after only one release but still live on through these recordings. If you like soul and country influenced rock and blues give The Breeze Band a listen. You may be pleasantly surprised to hear what five guys from the rez could come up with.

The 1-minute snippet you hear in the church choir scene in the movie \\"Letters to God\\" first reminded me of an acapella offering done in a sort of breezy \\"Manhattan Transfer\\"-ish confident style.    Yet as it continued, the acapella soprano soloist who sings a counterpoint (not sure of the actual musical term since I'm not a musician but that's how I think of it) really puts a bow on it and makes it truly special.  Her lilting, ethereal vocal accents had a sort of \\"Native American Indian Maiden\\" spirit quality to it - I know that's an odd description but that's the first impression I got when I first heard this passage.    The composer/arranger/conductor Derric Johnson is a genius in the complex yet immensely satisfying ending - it could have ended naturally enough with the group's vocal denouement, but then the soprano soloist takes it to another level with her own 7-8 notes, and you think it's over; but then the soloist carries it to yet another height when she takes it home with her closing 4 notes.  Just beautiful!  Musical perfection.    You don't have to be a religious person to appreciate the gorgeous musical artistry but it is a tribute that Derric matched such a beautiful vocal composition to such words.    After watching the movie, I had to go back to the \\"Scene Selection\\" feature and play that church choir scene about 10 times just to soak up that pure aural gold.     The acapella piece sounds like a recent modern jazzy creation; now here's the shocker - it was originally composed and performed back in 1964!    (As a bonus, if you play the movie with the Director and Writer commentary \\"On,\\" when they get to that scene they reveal that it is actually Derric Johnson playing the choirmaster in the movie and I believe they said some of his original singers were members of the movie choir!)

Kind of like if you took Orange Juice (the band) and Prefab Sprout, mixed in some Arctic Monkeys and Phoenix, added a cup of Orange Juice (the beverage) and blended it all together. product_title: Sir Lucious Left Foot...The Son Of Chico Dusty [Explicit]
review_body:
Sir Luscious Left Foot: The Son of Chico Dusty is the latest effort from Big Boi, one half of the hip-hop group Outkast. Outkast has always been known for their progressive and innovative style that pushes hip-hop music to new levels and challenges the genres stereotypes. Sir Luscious Left Foot continues the inventive tradition by implementing spaced-out soul, funk, and R&B into its heavy hitting beats.
The album begins with the track \\"Feel Me (Intro).\\" It's a short minute and a half piece that utilizes a reverberated whistle, auto tune chorus, deep piano and bass over a traditional southern rap drum beat. It does its job by drawing the listener in mystery and excitement about what's next.
While the album is heavy with guest appearances, \\"Daddy Fat Sacks,\\" the first full track of the album, features only Big Boi himself as a sort of \\"here I am, and here is what I do\\" song. Full of majestic synthesizers and electronic handclaps, it sets the tone for the powerful album that is to follow.
Veteran Outkast collaborators, Organized Noize, contribute to four standout tracks on Sir Luscious Left Foot. \\"Back Up Plan,\\" \\"For Your Sorrows,\\" \\"Turns Me On,\\" and \\"The Train pt. 2 (Sir Luscious Left Foot Saves the Day)\\" continue the space funk that Organized Noize has perfected and Sleepy Brown's vocals on \\"Turns me on\\" give the cool laid back vibe that the south is known for.
A collaboration with Outkast partner, Andre 3000, brings an interesting change to the albums sound. The track \\"You Ain't No DJ\\" is made up of a beat that sounds like banging on metal and laser shots. It is different from the other tracks in a minimalistic sense. It only utilizes a couple of sounds but still manages to hold the listeners attention. A guest appearance by Alabama Rapper YelaWolf on the track adds a welcoming switch from the norm.
Sir Luscious Left Foot: The Son of Chico Dusty was made over the course of a three-year period when Big Boi was working on other projects such as movies and his record label. When it was completed, it was put on hold by his former label Jive records, which claimed that Big Boi could not release that material under his new label Def Jam. There is rumor that Jive records originally believe the album was too \\"artsy\\" to have much commercial success and decided to shelve the work. Luckily for us listeners, the majority of the work during this period made it onto Sir Luscious Left Foot and resulted in one of the best hip-hop albums of 2010.as movies and his record label. Prime Cuts: Clouds, Oh Cumberland, A Cold, Rainy Morning in London in June

Like a moth to a flame, over the years many artists just flock to record Matraca Berg's compositions. These singers do come from the whole spectrum of genres including Linda Ronstadt (\\"Walk On\\"), Reba McEntire (\\"The Last One to Know\\"), Kenny Chesney and Grace Potter (\\"Me and Tequila\\"), Sara Evans (\\"Fool, I'm a Woman\\"), Trisha Yearwood (\\"Lying to the Moon\\") and Gretchen Wilson (\\"I Don't Feel Like Loving You Today\\"). A listen to Berg's first record in 13 years \\"The Dreaming Fields\\" will reveal the reasons why Berg has been such a much demanded scribe. Her songs unfold like juicy gossips from a women's magazine where she chronicles for us the stories of love, deceit, anguish, pain and the fear of getting old. Most importantly, Berg does not just sing; she makes us feel the emotions that brim beneath the surfaces of each track. Berg has a way of helping us feel that these are more than just songs. Rather, they are life stories coming out of the pages of our lives--some of which are so nebulously painful yet so profoundly articulated that they soothe our pains. Such is the beauty of this disc. But Berg is more than just a stellar writer, when she steps up to the microphone she is equally mesmerizing. Her plaintive tenor in her vocals emphatically draws us effortlessly into each syllable leaving a bittersweet aftertaste that becomes so alluring.

The tracks that do excel are the ballads, especially the heartbreaking kind. Thankfully, they exist here in spades. Check out the lonesome folk ballad \\"If I Had Wings,\\" a forlorn tale about an abused wife who finally had the courage to fight back. Despite the song's acoustic framed arrangement it can hardly masked the violent lyrics as Berg sings, \\"Mama said call a preacher, I just called the law/We all knew sooner or later/It was gonna be me or him...\\" In similar lines is the sultry bluesy \\"Your Husband's Cheating on Us\\" that also tells of infidelity but this time told from the perspective of the other woman. Berg vocally struts with such attitude that she could easily rival Reba McEntire on how to be a feisty yet classy diva. Calling to mind her classic ballad \\"Lying to the Moon,\\" the guitar and fiddled led \\"Clouds\\" has the same haunting and searing melancholy that just makes heartache feels so good. \\"South of Heaven\\" again is another emotional heavyweight as this time Berg is joined by her \\"Wine, Women and Song\\" road buddies Gretchen Peters and Suzy Bogguss on this anti-war song. What sets \\"South of Heaven\\" apart from the copious songs about war is that it is told through the eyes of a terrified mother who cries: \\"God you gave your only son, you are not the only one...\\"

Berg has resurrected two of her self-penned songs first recorded by her clients before. The first is the current single \\"Oh Cumberland,\\" a track that first appeared on Nitty Gritty Dirt Band's \\"Will the Circle Be Unbroken Vol. 3.\\" A song Berg wrote for a homesick friend who had just moved to LA, this is just therapeutic stuff for the hurting. The other cover is \\"You and Tequila\\" - the current single of Kenny Chesney and Grace Potter--here finds Berg drawing comparisons between the addiction of love and whiskey. Even darker moments come with \\"Silver and Glass\\" as Berg explores the inevitable fate of getting old. Of note also is the ruminative \\"A Cold, Rainy Morning in London in June\\" a wistful piano piece where the protagonist finds herself comparing to a lonely looking postcard. Despite the understated backings, the emotions here are stark, penetrating and they really go for the heart.

Perhaps a major quibble about this disc is that it's far too ballad driven. One certainly misses Berg in her more sassy moments a la on her debut RCA disc where she sings \\"I Got It Bad\\" and the \\"The Things You Left Undone.\\" Also a few tracks become far too indulgent and wordy including the pretty average \\"Racing the Angels.\\" Nevertheless, despite these challenges, \\"The Dreaming Fields\\" is still land worth visiting for its realistic presentation of love and its ensuing tragedies.heless, despite these challenges, \\"The Dreaming Fields\\" is still land worth visiting for its realistic presentation of love and its ensuing tragedies.

I've only played Halo 3 for a few hours at a friend's house, and only a fraction of it was campaign.     And yet, I love this music. Some soundtracks are only good once you've seen the movie/played the game (like the Inception OST). However, this album stands alone quite nicely.    It starts out with Luck, a quiet, noble track tinged with reminiscent sadness. Then, the tracks slowly build in intensity. Halfway up this build is Out of Shadow, taking full advantage of stereo sound and electronic beat to create a subtle but extremely pleasing rhythm. Later comes a peak, This Is the Hour, a heroic variation on the main Halo theme, which then subsides into chilling darkness for the track Dread Intrusion. However, the music becomes more positive and epic through Follow Our Brothers, Farthest Outpost, Behold a Pale Horse, and Three Gates. The creepy beginning of Black Tower segues into an sad and emotional second  half, followed soon by the touching Keep What You Steal. The beautiful choral music at the beginning of Halo Reborn is echoed in Greatest Journey, which then becomes the main Halo theme. And boy, what a theme it is. Greatest Journey is the climax of the entire album. Tribute and Roll Call have the general feeling of victory, but not without sadness and sacrifice and remembrance. Wake Me When You Need Me is a quiet, emotional track, echoing many of the tones of Luck and bringing the album full-circle. Finally, extras are tacked onto the end, including the beautiful track Never Forget, a slow and emotional mix of three subtle themes.    And soon, all too soon, the music is over.     So, you play it again! :D    It's epic, it's subtle, it is the compilation of Marty O'Donnell's work on Halo 1 and Halo 2, and it surpasses both.     Plus, look at the value! Over thirty excellent songs for only nine dollars? A must-buy for anyone interested in soundtrack music.

review_headline: What can I say?  Decades of Mellow, Swinging Perfection
review_body: I've always liked the Mills Brothers.  As a child I liked the bounce and fun of \\"Glow Worm\\" - but over the years the acapella gifts of this group is something I've appreciated more and more.  The mix is a little uneven, but these are 100 great songs from a group that spanned years of styles.  It starts with Tiger Rag - the Brothers used to put on every record, \\"No musical instruments or mechanical devices used on this recording other than one guitar\\" - and ends up with Big Band arrangements and even a touch of rock and roll sounds.  (Thank heaven that's minimal).    But for the purist, the person that wants to hear the close harmonies of the original four brothers, there is still a lot of material.  One of the fun things about listening to them is marveling at their ability to mimic instruments - fully displayed on songs like \\"Caravan\\" and \\"Nobody's Sweetheart\\".  If you want the popular swinging classics, check out \\"Glow Worm\\" (two versions) or Paper Doll.  Me, I'm a sucker for the pure old harmonies with guitar or a simple piano- I cried the first time I heard \\"Let Me Call You Sweetheart\\".  It's just so beautiful, and I'm a sap for real beauty.  A bonus on this album are some guest stars - Ella Fitzgerald is noted, but Al Jolson and Bing aren't.    Some of the older songs have a case of the crackles but you expect that.  This is a good selection.  If harmony,  tunefulness, and real mastery are what you look for in an album, try this one.  It works out to about 9 cents a song, and there are very few clunkers here.  You really can't go wrong.

I once had this band's demo on a cassette...waaay back in the 90's.   I held little hope for ever finding those songs in any other format since I think I only heard Stompbox played once on 101 KLOL in Houston before KLOL went Latino (End of an Era, my Droobs...). I wore out that cassette, and have long wished to hear this band's tight, percussive, differently-choppy style again. Few groups from my days as a student of Audio Engineering have ever touched the precision of the riff/drum/bass phrases that these guys put together. The vocals stand (in my not so humble opinion) among the finest of the era, whilst being drowned out by pop-like, retro-punk-grunge fare latched onto by the masses. Don't get me wrong, I liked that stuff too. A lot.   However, Stompbox provided me a heady sense of satisfaction every time I pushed Play on my tape deck to share it at high volume with friends, as my pals had never heard something quite like Stompbox before. My friends thought it was cool that I had found this semi-rare treasure within the confines of the Outer-Houston area, and by extention I became one or two iotas cooler every time I heard a friend or acquaintance murmur \\"Whoah! Who the #*@% are those guys?!?\\".   I thouroughly recommend Stompbox as a rare, satisfying treat to the ear-holes of all who may enjoy a departure from the regular 90's era rock music form.

'Bingo' was a fantastic CD release last year by the talented legendary blues rock band, The Steve Miller Band. Expectations therefore may be very high on their 2011 follow-up/new CD release titled 'Let Your Hair Down'. The MP3 download has only 10 tracks (no 4 bonus tracks here as in CD unfortunately) & opens with the track \\"Snatch It Back And Hold It\\" : a great blues track with great vocals & music sounding like a 'live performance'. Other great tracks include \\"I Got Love If You Want It\\", \\"Just A Little Bit\\", \\"Close Together\\" (great vocals & harmony and the blues sound reminiscent of The Jeff Heally Band), \\"No More Doggin'\\", \\"Can't Be Satisfied\\", \\"Sweet Home Chicago\\" (a great saxophone infused blues track with great vocals) & \\"Love The Life I Live\\" (great guitar & melody). Two tracks stand-out for me namely \\"Pretty Thing\\" (up-tempo track, wonderful music, melody & vocals. This is my favourite track from this CD) & \\"The Walk\\" (beautiful guitar & great vocals. The song reminiscent to Prince's \\"It's The Walk\\" from his blues/jazz 1999's release by Warner Brothers titled 'The Vault : All Friends For Sale' but this one by The Steve Miller Band is a better track). On overall, this is a good CD release effort by The Steve Miller Band & deserves three and half stars, a recommended CD listening.

I enjoyed Nathan's music when he was part of Celtae, so naturally I was looking forward to his solo release, 'Lovers, Leavers and Believers'.    I wasn't disappointed.    He's both an accomplished musician and lyricist. In fact, 'Till I met your Sister' may be worth the cost of the CD all on it's own.  I mean, how can you beat \\"Baby I was game to be your mister / until I met your sister.\\"     The exquisite ballad 'That Week in Montreal\\" starts with a lovely picked guitar and flows through to a melancholy remembrance of a week in, well, Montreal.     The anthem \\"I Just Wanna Know\\" rips through to it's conclusion far too soon. (I could listen to that on repeat for hours.) \\"4 Cups of Coffee\\" should be on the radio. Now (and if I can do anything about it, it will be.) review_headline: Nashville country duo sings with terrific passion
review_body: Keith Burns (previously of Trick Pony) and Michelle Poe form this unabashedly mainstream Nashville duet, but beneath the grooming, market trending and AOR production, you can hear real passion in their vocals. Burns sings with the husked edge of Don Henley (and the chiseled looks of a model) while Poe has a clear, soulful tone that works both as a lead and harmony voice. Their material doesn't break any new ground - sunny days, broken hearts, the healing power of love and a man's love of trucks - but their talent and enthusiasm are truly infectious. Beyond the singles (\\"Don't Get No Better Than That,\\" \\"How Long is Long Enough?\\" and \\"Second Chance\\") there are many rewarding album tracks, including the sharp kiss-off \\"Life's Too Short\\" and the bluesy rocker \\"Gone as All Get Out.\\" The fourteen tracks are split between two CDs, with the second disc given over to duet arrangements. The latter disc opens with the conversational back-and-forth of \\"Second Chance\\" and culminates in a live medley that salutes Kenny & Dolly, David & Shelly and Sonny & Cher. Producer Mark Oliverius balances the interests of radio and roots, mixing big guitars with quieter twang (including some chiming 12-string on \\"Move On\\"), showcasing the vocalists on everything from power ballads to gentle weepers. Burns and Poe are talented singers with an artistic vision that's polished, but not subverted, by Nashville's commercial demands. [©2011 hyperbolium dot com]

\\"Heartbeats\\" and \\"Quick Escapes\\" both have a radio-friendly feel -- in fact, the latter is the first radio single from the EP -- whereas \\"Push Away\\" has already been remixed at least once, and \\"Out Of Touch\\" would feel perfect in a post-goth dance club as is. I was surprised when playing a new TAPE to hear his dreamy version of this.  A few years back he came thru Birmingham and had a little showing 2 nights in a small theatre setting.  His commentary on this song was that if you are going to sing something, it should be something pretty. \\"And this is a pretty song.\\" He is not much interested in mixing with the crowd; looks like he might be irritated easily.  I forgive him all when he sings this, and he did at this mini-concert.  It is a haunting melody, complete with the strange vocals only Leon has. This one is amazing. I can picture myself on the beach,  intially laying on a hammock until she tells me to walk to the water's edge... then I am standing at the shoreline, staring at the waves, picking up shells, eventually night falls and there is a crackling fireplace that is very calming and soothing and I swear I can smell the burning wood... this is the first time I've ever gotten completely into one of these tapes and after 20 minutes I feel so relaxed. I've begun to do this meditation for a few minutes before work too but my favorite is to lay down for 20 minutes after a hard day at work and relax in this island paradise. I wish calmsound would produce other guided meditations because this one is the best I've found so far.

The title \\"Greatest\\" is a bit misleading since the focus here is the Brothers Gibb's biggest hits during their oft maligned disco era on the RSO label, from 1975's \\"Jive Talkin\\" (the leadoff track) to 1979's \\"Love You Inside Out.\\" There's nothing here from the earlier phase of their career on the Atco label or that post-dates 1979, and only a handful that showcases great album tracks not released as singles like \\"You Stepped Into My Life,\\" \\"Wind of Change\\" and \\"Children of the World.\\" While the Bee Gees didn't invent disco they certainly were one of its leading proponents and \\"Greatest\\" oddly excises two tracks that were Top 40 hits during this era like 1977's \\"Boogie Child\\" and \\"Edge of the Universe.\\" But the big disco hits are all here in all their ear-shattering falsettoed glory. It's easy to stereotype what's here as vapid mindless disco, but if you look deeper \\"Greatest\\" showcases some of songwriting's greatest hooks. If you're looking to get your disco on \\"Greatest\\" is a great place to start.

review_headline: Shades of Alan Jackson, George Strait and Randy Travis
review_body: This album is essentially a showcase for the songs of \\"Country Music\\" songwriter and record producer, Lawrence John, who divides his time between the twinned cities of Nashville, Tennessee and Belfast, Northern Ireland.  A native of Belfast, Lawrence has had a lifelong interest in Country music and enjoyed several stints as a Country deejay, playing classic american Country music and interviewing legends like Johnny Cash and Charley Pride.  His love of and knowledge of \\"Country\\", stand him in good stead, in this, his first collection of self penned songs.  As someone who neither sings or plays any instruments himself, Lawrence employs a core group of three Nashville singers and a bunch of Nashville super pickers, to bring life to his songs, which he serves up in a variety of styles, ranging from Neo Traditional Country and Tex Mex to Bluegrass, or as he calls it Greengrass, Irish songs played Bluegrass style.  A perfect example of this is, \\"Remember Those Trips\\", Lawrence's nostalgic recollection of childhood trips with his family, through the famous Glens of Antrim to Ballycastle and Portrush.  In contrast, \\"Angel At The Station Inn\\", is a slice of pure American country, inspired by a Monday night visit to Nashville's famous Station Inn.  And while there are shades of Randy Travis about this track, Alan Jackson is definitely the first name which comes to mind on hearing, \\"WWW. She Stole My Heart\\", a cleverly told tale of \\"love at first sight\\" in an internet cafe.  Equally clever lyrics can be found in, \\"Heavenly\\", which has a distinct George Strait feel to it. This song was written for Irish singer John McNicoll, who had a big radio hit with it in Ireland.  Another song which received extensive radio play in Ireland and also in Spain, when recorded by country singer-songwriter Cliff Austin, is \\"Today, Tomorrow And Always\\", a clear musical nod to the Eagles.  The more traditional, \\"We Got Country\\", a brief history of how country music has evolved from it's roots into what it is today, was written as a duet,  specially for Country legend George Jones and Irish Country star Mike Denver.  An unusual blend of Irish and Spanish music provides the soundtrack for the \\"close to the truth\\" story of how \\"Single Irish Girls\\" behave on their Spanish holidays these days, effectively turning the tables on the Spanish romeos of old, who would to prey on naive young Irish girls holidaying far away from home.  Other songs on the album include, the Tex Mex track \\"Crazy Over You\\", the more contemporary country track \\"I Wanna Love You All Night Long\\", the obligatory \\"cheatin' song\\", \\"I'll Never Cheat Again\\" and an acoustic track, \\"Little Friend\\", Lawrence's poignant tribute to his dog Lobo, who died in January 2009. (well it is a country album)  Yep, it's a country album alright and though the songs and musical styles are quite diverse, the consistant production feel seems to hold it all together nicely to make what is effectively, a well balanced and melodically enjoyable listening experience.    *****Credit also, to Lawrence's arranger, studio engineer and steel player, Gary Carter, who early in his career played with Lorrie Morgan, then spent ten years as music director and steel player for Randy Travis, before 3 years as music director for Faith Hill and then Connie Smith as music director and steel player.    Sleeve notes mention a 2008 Cliff Austin album, \\"Belfast To Nashville\\", produced by Lawrence, a forthcoming debut album he's producing for 24 year old Nashville singer Keri Hemingway, \\"Honky Tonks And Heartaches\\" due in December 2009 and another \\"Project\\" album \\"God and \\"Country\\".

review_headline: News songs, Missing Songs, Terrible Songs......Pity!
review_body:
First off......I must admit that the two new tracks \\"Almost Over\\" and \\"Magic Man\\" are really good songs, however, I wonder if they are truly new written songs or leftover tracks from the Hell To Pay and/or Lightning Strikes Again sessions? Why is really doesn't matter, I am just curious because these two new songs maintain the essence of the two previous albums with Levin.

Now......the rest of the album. Man, this is hard. Being a longtime Dokken fan it is really difficult to judge this without being to cynical.
Initially, all the guitars, drums, bass work on the re-recorded tunes are pretty good.....with the exception of some strange chords, and off-tempos here and there... I give the musicianship of the re-recorded tracks a 85/100. I can honestly say that Dream Warriors is a 1/2 step too slow and it bored me...they ruined it IMO.

The vocals.... what in the world is going on here? Besides Don's two new tracks (which are up to par with LSA & HTP), the rest are junk and too painful to listen to. It sounds like he is straining and pushing too hard......no passion and enthusiasm behind the lead tracks here. It appears to be almost lazy demo quality vocals here. I am disappointed with the re-recorded lead vocals tracks...not to mention that the backing vocals are all over the place - and are not harmonized with the lead tracks...... I am sorry but the vocals on the re-recorded tracks I would have to give a 50/100.

Although, the two new tracks...overall I would rate them at a 89/100.

Obviously, what is missing here is the other two new tracks or cover tunes.......where are they in the Amazon & iTunes releases? Are they now reserved for the overseas (Japan) releases now? I have done some digging around the internet and various cd sites....and really no one has a definitive track listing; some have the 4 new tracks and some only have the 2 originals. Personally, I have heard the original two cover tunes...and can say that if Dokken did not mess around too much with the arrangements - they could be pretty solid and worth listening too if they indeed will be on the final official release......which would be worth (IMHO) buying the physical disc when released.

NOTE: the cover of the GH2......for you Dokken fanatics...is in fact the original cover for Hell to Pay for the Japanese release only....which was a limited pressing and then redone to match the North American releaseuch with the arrangements - they could be pretty solid and worth listening too if they indeed will be on the final official release......which would be worth (IMHO) buying the physical disc when released. I've been a fan of Harlequin since their very fine album, Love Crimes, from the early eighties.  Like many bands from that decade, they fell off the radar and for all purposes were defunct.  Happily, they cranked out \\"Waking the Jester\\" a few years ago.  I'm sorry I didn't catch it when it was first released, but better late than never.  As I said in the title, this has very little in common with their early efforts, and that's a good thing.  As much as I like Love Crimes, this album stands alongside it as a great companion although there is little similarity between them, at least on the surface.  Waking the Jester boasts a much harder sound, leaving the pop sensibilities of their earlier incarnation in the dust as they pursue a modern growl that persists throughout.  The guitars are low and thunderous, the vocals are tough, and the songs demand attention.  That said, they haven't lost complete touch with their roots.  Vocal harmonies are present more often than not, and every song packs a nice hook that makes the album immediate and memorable.  Good production, great songs, excellent execution... It deserves far more accolades than it will ever get.  For those who are debating the purchase, you may consider this private stock and money well spent.  Enjoy, and spread the word.

The excellent use of stereo gives this recording pleasing depth and a sense of dimension like one might experience sitting on a deserted beach listening to gently crashing waves. It's an easy and painless way to meditate. This particular recording is also excellent for de-stressing after a particularly onerous day at work. It's certainly cheaper than psychotherapy! Anyway, if you enjoy natural rhythmic soundscapes as a relaxation aid, I highly recommend Ocean Waves. It's the best beach around without the crowds, sand, and sunburn.

Here it is, all of your ballroom practice music needs on one disc. Nothing is more  frustrating than paying sixty dollars an hour for a private ballroom lesson and then  spending half of that time digging through CD's trying to find appropriate practice  tempo music. I can't count the number of times I've wasted most of a practice session  scrounging around trying to find a good song. Now, there are two things I take to every  practice session: my dance shoes and this CD. This CD is the ultimate \\"Swiss Army Knife\\"  of dance practice music.  These tracks are \\"basic beat\\" music at an easy beginner tempo. Finding practice-tempo  music is almost impossible because all of the ballroom music producers use the rather  fast \\"standard\\" tempos dictated by dance competition rules.  Most good teaching studios  have variable speed controls on the CD player to allow slowing the tempo for beginners.   But, unfortunately, many do not.  Learning to dance is tough enough without the frustration of digging around trying to  find music and practicing with tempos that are too fast. Note: the tracks in this CD set  are not popular, \\"original artist,\\" commercially available selections.  Instead, they  are rather nondesrcipt pieces. So, if you are looking for really hot music, keep  looking.  For specialty CD's like this one, I wish they would include the manufacturer's liner  notes and product description. Since they do not, I will write an except here:  \\"This album contains basic instrumental rhythm tracks for practicing ballroom dancing.  These are not typical \\"songs.\\" Instead, these highlight the distinct rhythm style of  each ballroom dance. This one album contains every rhythm style for both American style  and International style ballroom.\\"

After 3 years away from the scene, I was thrilled to hear of new songs coming out from the person who used to be my all time favorite musician Christian or non-Christian period. However, when I heard all of the songs, I must say I was extremely disappointed.     I know everyone is saying that this cd is Joy's true self, but, in my honest opinion, it actually sounds like every other female vocal bursting onto the scene these days. In fact, I'm almost convinced that if a female artist wants to make it big she better have an alto/second soprano voice and know how to play the piano. Now, I understand that Joy has always been a very gifted piano player and I love the intimate, heartfelt touch it added in songs like \\"Every Moment\\" and \\"Do They See Jesus\\" on previous albums. Nonetheless, that doesn't mean I want to hear someone as so versatile as Joy Williams sounding the same on every single track in a way that sounds like a mediocre imitation of other piano driven female artists. For me, Joy just doesn't cut it the same way someone like Sara Bareilles or Francesca Battistelli does. In fact, there are some points in the songs when I absolutely want to cover my ears because her vocals are just too contrived. She does it well in some songs, but before the second song ends, I'm done with the bland vibe that starts to resonate.     This is not the Joy Williams I remember. I'm happy that she's happy and feels that she's \\"growing\\" as an artist, but I am just very disappointed and find myself moving on. If this EP is any indication of what's to come, then I won't be adding any more Joy to my collection. The reason I give this EP a 3 stars is because it has one very decent song, \\"One of Those Days\\" and it's so good and reminiscient of the Joy Williams I've come to love as an artist, that it doesn't surprise me they chose to title the EP the same and make it the first track. I wish all the best to Joy Williams and while I may not enjoy this EP, I hope that it and future songs released continue to light the darkness of this world.

review_headline: White Dreams with Style and Heart
review_body:
Prime Cuts: Erika's Song, The Little Things, Dustbowl Dreams

Bryan White was the poster child of country music of the 90s. His smashing boyish good looks, his wafting tenor, and his streamlined mainstream pop country were the prerequisites for stardom during the post-Garth Brooks climate of the nineties. Certainly White was devoured by radio, resulting in a stream of hits, 4 of which even reached the Billboard chart's penthouse. They include \\"Rebecca Lynn,\\" \\"Sittin' on Go,\\" \\"Someone Else's Star,\\" and \\"So Much for Pretending.\\" Unfortunately, loyalty has never been the earmark of country radio. Prior to the turn of the new millennium, hits were drying up and after 1999's \\"How Lucky I Am,\\" Lady Luck was no longer on White's side. 10 years of exile in the land without the support of a major label, White is back with this independently released \\"Dustbowl Dreams.\\" Stripping away the gloss that often comes with a major label product, \\"Dustbowl Dreams\\" finds White adopting a more hands-on approach. With him and band mate Derek George not only helming the CD themselves, but White has a hand in co-penning all the tracks, save for three.

While in the 90s, White has been spoon fed with a few padded froth (such as \\"Eugene the Genius\\"), this time round he searches his soul for some heart rendering compositions. Best of which is the title cut \\"Dustbowl Dreams.\\" An eloquent autobiographical entry from the viewpoint of the \\"son of the son of an auctioneer\\" detailing their life, struggles and perseverance, this is a slice of Americana that ought to speak to anyone who has had struggles in life. Such personal investments also show with \\"Erika's Song,\\" a song White wrote about his wife Erika. Backed by a bevy of lush strings over the romantic tingling of the piano, this is White at his romantic best calling to mind his career highlight duet with Shania Twain \\"From This Moment On.\\" Lead single \\"The Little Things\\" is a sonic chicken soup for the soul, here finding White giving thanks for all the often overlooked things in life from yellow post-it notes from his beloved to tiny babies. Though not written by White (but by Daly Blair and Derek George), \\"On My Own\\" is perhaps his autobiographical apology for his hiatus from music in the last 10 years or so--a dark brooding burner about the loneliness of living an itinerant life on the road.

A few tracks tackle perennial issues often dealt with in country music: alcoholism and its devastating effects is the theme of \\"When You Come Around.\\" What is to be commended about \\"When You Come Around\\" is White's earnest plea to his dad to wake up from his sordid stupor. \\"Beautiful Place,\\" on the other hand, is your average island getaway piece that really falls flat as White's strained tenor just doesn't have that tropical lilt. Avid fans can also testify that White is not just a vocalist but he's also a guitarist par excellence. Partnering with buddy Steve Wariner, \\"Hands of Time\\" is more a guitar show-off piece with his lightning speed riffs than anything. While \\"Say When\\" is obligatory positive love up-tempo number that sounds like it belongs to the Bryan White's 90s catalogue without the catchiness of \\"Sittin' on Go.\\"

After 10 years, it's good to see a new Bryan White CD back on the shelves. But more than just a CD, there is more personal investments on White's part. He is more open this time to share his life on disc. Especially on the ballad front, Bryan White still croons with style and heart. review_headline: What Would I Do Without Amazon
review_body: If it wasn't for Amazon, this would be a song that I heard once and never again. I heard it in a TV show one night and it was very good, as is the case with a lot of TV, they did not run credits. It sounded like Willie Nelson, his un-mistaken phrasing obvious. So I went to Amazon and found it. I also discovered that it was written by Bob Dylan. It's a great song but I like the Willie treatment, he Willie-izes the song and makes it his. As with any well written song it hooks you and doesn't let go. It's haunting melody sticks with you and nags at you to remember the rest of the words. It leaves you wanting more, wishing there was one more verse and chorus in a never ending loop to play over and over.       I don't know about the rest of the country, but the Atlanta area radio market is dead. There are no adult current rock stations, for some reason they think that all we want to listen to is 1970's Fleetwood Mac, Eagles and Bob Seger. There are rap, country, oldies, and power rock stations. But what about jazz, classical, easy listening and some form of new releases by old artists. This song is not the usual Willie country song so it would not be played on a country station. If you get a chance it is worth a listen.

review_headline: Still Sounds Good After So Many Years
review_body: When I was 15 (back in 1985), I had the good fortune to start working at the local radio station in my hometown of Andrews, TX.  I worked weekends and on Sunday morning, I got to play Christian Music.  My job was to play records from 6am until 10am then air the church services of the two largest churches in town.  I really didn't know anything about Christian Pop/Rock music at that time, so I was playing about 2 or 3 records that I liked by Dallas Holm and Amy Grant over and over again.  After a couple of weeks, this guy walked into the station with a huge stack of records and \\"How the West Was One\\" was among them.  I had never heard of Phil Keaggy, but he was one of my favorite artists from the moment I played this record.  He is even better live than he is on his studio albums, that is what makes this recording so special.  2nd Chapter of Acts is Great live too.  Matthew Ward has probably the most amazing voice of any male vocalist I have ever heard!

First of all, I am a huge fan of Tobymac, as well as his alumnus dc Talk. I will primarily comparing this album to [[ASIN:B000MGUZRU Portable Sounds]] (check out my review over there) since it's the only other full Tobymac album I have. This album is much electronic than PS, it also has better rap and lots of it. Portable Sounds has very little in the way of rap. There are also better guest appearances on this album. Toby's faith is shown clearly on this masterpiece. PS was more guitary, whereas Tonight is much more hip-hop, rap sounding. Here is a song breakdown:

Tonight feat. John Cooper of Skillet: A decent opener, the tune is pretty catchy. The lyrics are about turning back to Christ for your faith. Toby really boned in one area though. John Cooper doesn't have his own verse!!! You can hear him in the chorus, quite clearly if you pay attention, because his voice distinctly gravelly. Other than that, this one is great.

Get Back Up: Comparable to Face of the Earth from PS, or Death Story from After the Music Stops by Lecrae. Nice beat, with lots of drumming. Lyrics are being down and out, and God helping you get back into life.

Funky Jesus Music feat. Beckah Shae and Siti Monroe: Amazing song! Very electronic sound. Sweet beat. The ladies do a phenomenal job with the chorus and intro. Siti Monroe also appeared in \\"One World\\" from PS. About not wanting to listen to secular, non-God-honoring music, but rather, \\"that funky Jesus Music\\". Lyrics are similar to \\"Jesus Muzik\\" by Lecrae.

City On Our Knees: This is the highly acclaimed single released several months ago. A very slow, soft beat. Fewer drums. About the sharing the Gospel, and then going with all the believers to \\"a city on our knees\\" (heaven), \\"with one king\\" (God). Really nice incorporation of some strings in the second verse. I'm not so sure that this is the exact version released in August, because this one is longer. Similar lyrics to \\"One World\\" from Portable Sounds.

ShowStopper: This song is phenomenal!!!! The best rap from Toby on this album. This is the only song that has extended use of guitars. Whenever I listen to this song, I am reminded of the old Nu Thang days twenty years ago (think \\"Walls\\"). About missions. Similar lyrics to Lecrae's \\"Send Me\\".

Changed Forever feat. Nirva Ready: Nifty song. Nirva is great on the chorus. Not really like anything I've ever heard before, but still great. About coming face-to-face with Jesus, and being changed forver. Nice hip-hop beat. This song is the only other one that really incorporates guitars.

Hold On: The intro is a great little pipe organ solo. No rap, but Toby shows his vocal talent. About a friend who's down in the dumps, and Toby tells her that he still loves her, and that God does too, with an unchanging love, and that the two of them need to follow Him. Similar, lyrically, to \\"I'm for You\\" from PS.

Loud 'n' Clear (truDog '10): Oh, man, truDog rocks! He is AWESOME! He's a big reason why Toby's albums rank so highly with me. This is the first truDog that I really felt was a song, and not just a little kid messing around in his dad's studio. This kid has a bright future ahead of him in the CCM industry.

Hey Devil: This is a really great song, essentially telling Satan to get his conniving rear outta here. Whenever I listen to this song I continually think \\"Newsboys\\". It could possibly be a sort of tribute, since dc Talk took Newsboys under their wing when they (Newsboys) came to the States, and now Toby's former band member Michael Tait is the lead singer of the 'Boys. If you've heard \\"Giving it Over\\" from Thrive by the Newsboys, you'll have a sense of how this song sounds.

Wonderin' Feat. Matthew Thiessen: Essentially a bio of Toby, from DCT to now. Softer and slower. Matt Thiessen, of Relient K, doesn't have his own verse, but he still does a good job.

Captured: A really neat song. A bit slower, but the lyrics are great. They're about being captured by Christ's glory. The best song lyrically on the entire album.

Start Somewhere: This song is sweet! A catchy Mexican-sounding tune, complete with trumpets and everything. About a struggling relationship. Toby says that God is the only one that can help the realationship get better.

Break Open The Sky feat. Israel Houghton: Toby teams up again with Israel (they produced a song for CompassionArt) to round out this album, except for the remixes. Essentially a prayer that Jesus would come back to earth, and take all the Christians home. Israel has his own verse (surprise), which he performs well. Slower, but still good.

City on Our Knees (Radio Edit) Not much to say here. A slight change in sound, and for the better, in my opinion.

I got the deluxe version, so here's the review of the extra songs that came with it.

Captured (KP Reimix) A bit more upbeat than the original, with the same lyrics.

Hold On (Telemitry Remix) More electronic that the original. I think it's better.

Tonight (New Day Remix) A downgrade from the original. It flows more smoothly though.

Overall, this is a great album. Don't neccesarily think that because you liked Portable Sounds, you'll like this. It's completely new and different. Enjoy!est song lyrically on the entire album. I was introduced to the music of Bettye LaVette via Atlantic vinyl LPs, but she's been singing since the '60s. And unlike a lot of singers who made it big, she still sings. Her voice is comparable to that of Tina Turner or Aretha Franklin at their heyday, but her R&B and soul is all her own.     This single is a good introduction to her sound, plus the I-will-not-back-down theme of her repertoire.

Judging from her song \\"Adore\\", this is for any one who appreciates a good singer and good music, Jaci has an excellent voice. You may, like myself, listen to nearly all types of music. If any of her other songs are equal to \\"Adore\\" I recommend anything she sings.    However.... keep in mind that this is also available on the mp3 download album \\"Greatest Hits\\". Don't dowload it twice like I did.

review_headline: Chants that many modern music fans can appreciate
review_body: I first heard demos of Jdavyd's work on Myspace, and kept track of his progress as he worked on these recordings. Hearing the final results, I'm very impressed. Although I'm not familiar with devotional chanting as a formal genre, the strength of Jdavyd's voice and the depth of the arrangements carry the songs across barriers. I could easily see anyone interested in secular world-influenced music, like Dead Can Dance or Hedningarna, being a fan of this album. Jdavyd weaves electronic and acoustic instruments together with ease, and the album as a whole is quite sonically rich. Highly recommended.

For anyone growing up to the sounds of the Sutherland Brothers and Quiver in the '70s, this long-awaited solo-album is a really big surprise indeed. Gavin Sutherland took years to make it, but when he finally set down to it, he got so into things that he decided to sing and play all the parts himself. Seeing as the SBQ were never a very succesfull band in terms of album sales, it is no wonder that he decided to even distribute it himself. If you want the full album including the two bonus tracks Big storm blowin' and Where would I be, you can order it through [...]. And I can promise you the two extra songs are worth it.   Througout the whole album, Gavin Sutherland sounds much younger than his years. He bounces and bops, sooths and rocks and thereby gives each cut that extra push that distinguishes it from most things you will hear on the radio. Your favorite station will probaly not let you listen to this particular music, but if you don't pick it up yourself you'll surely miss a great deal.

review_headline: Finally the new album is here
review_body:
Like other reviewers here I'd already purchased a few of the songs that are included in this new album. It seems like it's been quite a while ago that I actually made a few of those purchases and that is probably not far from the truth as this album took a while to finally hit the streets. Now that it is here though, I can sit back and enjoy the tunes that have joined the earlier releases.

Josh Turner's voice is perfect for the songs he sings and was clearly destined for music. While he might have been able to serve as an announcer or emcee, to not have him singing would have been a waste of talent.

Turner's music easily straddles the seemingly ever-present fence between gospel and country with family friendly music, even in his romantic tunes things are suggestive at best and most of the romance is left to the listener's imagination.

This deluxe edition includes a few songs already included elsewhere, though given the number of tunes that are included those bonuses help make buying this version instead of the standard version a no-brainer.

The second track \\"King of Kings\\" blew me away.  I fancy myself a decent musician, and I have to say the quality with which this track is put together blows my mind. product_title: Praise: Integrity Music's Scripture Memory Songs
review_body: I first heard Integrity's Scripture Memory Songs years ago but lost my tapes.  Some of the songs stayed with me for over 20 years!  When I found them again on Amazon I was elated.  I LOVE the song, \\"In God We Make Our Boast.\\" Give it a listen and see if it doesn't just send your heart soaring.  The arrangements are so professionally done that I would expect this caliber of music on a much bigger budget project, but here it is with the Word of God.  How incredible!  And the vocalists they chose for each song are not your run-of-the-mill Christian singers.  They have such character to their voices and are gifted to do what they are doing.  In short, I LOVE  these cds and will definitely buy more.  If you want to get the Word of God in your heart AND you are a musician who appreciates quality, then these are for you!

I'm the first one reviewing this? Maybe it's because everyone else who heard it is still in shock. Before I started buying music online, I used to visit my neighborhood used CD shop. The owner would always give me brief but accurate assessments of the CD's I had selected for purchase, such as \\"That's a good one\\" or \\"That one stinks.\\" Terse, I admit, but he was seldom wrong. I not going to mince words either-this one stinks. It's the Tord Gustavsen ENSEMBLE, meaning the trio with a vocalist and sax player added. That initially sounded interesting to me-I loved the last three Tord Gustavsen trio albums, though I thought it was time for him to try something a little different. This, however, sounds like uninspired, meandering mush with an excruciatingly painful vocalist, Kristin Asbjornsen. The audio samples do not truly reflect how dreadful this is.
She sounds like Kim Carnes with a sore throat. I felt sorry for the poor dear and wanted to give her a throat lozenge halfway through the disk. Hey, I like most hoarse vocalist- Marianne Faithfull, Tom Waits, Peter Hammill screaming, whatever, but I can't stomach this. Some of the songs attempt to infuse the poetry of W.H. Auden, whom Kristen manages to make sound like a bad beat poet. That said,there are a few good moments musically on this album, (I counted two) and with another vocalist, say Susanne Abbuehl, Norma Winstone or even Annette Peacock this might have worked somewhat better. \\"Restored, Returned\\" is disappointing effort from a great musician. Skip this and buy one of his earlier albums or Stefano Bollani Trio's \\" Stone In The Water\\" instead. You'll be glad you did.

The CD is well paced, taking a break from the energizing, grin inducing, breakneck speed tunes to play gorgeous and introspective ballads.  Their skill as a team can not be beat, each of them having earned recognition and huge amounts of respect as solo performers and both having won the National Championship Title at the prestigious Walnut Valley Festival in Winfield Kansas. review_body: Middle School Principal Qadir Dixon has come up with a formula for success, and proves it with the release of this amazing music done by his students.
